g.text: Shortest talk first? Earliest start? Pick the rule.
Same four talks, one room per rule.
A talk may start the minute another ends.
Talks: A 0–10, B 1–4, C 3–5, D 4–7. One room.
Which rule fits the most talks?
2. Explore: after "Book next in every room"
Shortest talk first? Earliest start? Pick the rule.
Same four talks, one room per rule.
A talk may start the minute another ends.
Two rooms are full after one talk; one is not.
Its own Book next is the only enabled control left.
Reveal button: disabled until every room is full.
3. Reveal (stage pinned: all three rooms full)
Shortest talk first? Earliest start? Pick the rule.
Same four talks, one room per rule.
A talk may start the minute another ends.
Earliest start took A (0–10): 1 talk, room full.
Shortest took C (3–5); it clashed with B and D: 1 talk.
Earliest finish took B, which ended at 4, so D (4–7)
still fit: 2 talks. B, C and D overlap in pairs and
A clashes with all, so no room holds 3.
Ending first leaves the most day for what is left,
and swapping it in never makes a schedule worse.
